previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with recurrent primary central nervous system lymphoma was admitted for his 21st cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy as part of reinduction therapy. He presented in stable condition, reporting only mild port site irritation, and tolerated the methotrexate infusion well without acute complications. His hospital course was complicated by mild hyponatremia (lowest sodium 130), likely due to the interaction between intravenous fluids and desmopressin for his diabetes insipidus. Given the mild nature and lack of symptoms, desmopressin was continued, with expectation of correction after IV fluid cessation. Methotrexate levels declined appropriately to 0.08, and leucovorin rescue was administered as planned. He remained neurologically stable, seizure-free, and hemodynamically normal. He was discharged home with instructions to resume all home medications, discontinue leucovorin and bicarbonate, and follow up in clinic for Rituxan and MRI-based treatment planning.
